```bash
cd "/Users/karolinegriesbach/Documents/Innkeepr/Git/evaluation-and-execution-scripts/Evaluations/Tchibo-DV360/20260624" && python3 << 'EOF'
import pandas as pd
import glob
from pathlib import Path

data_dir = Path(".")
files = sorted(glob.glob(str(data_dir / "*.xlsx")))

all_line_items = set()
all_creative_groups = set()
pairs = set()

for f in files:
    df = pd.read_excel(f, skiprows=7)
    df = df.dropna(subset=["Line Item"], how="all")
    if "Line Item" not in df.columns:
        print(f"Missing Line Item in {f}, cols: {list(df.columns)}")
        continue
    df = df[df["Line Item"].notna()]
    df = df[df["Line Item"] != "Totals"]
    print(f"\n=== {Path(f).name} ===")
    print(f"Columns: {list(df.columns)}")
    print(f"Time col: {[c for c in df.columns if c in ['Week','Day']]}")
    line_items = df["Line Item"].unique()
    print(f"Line items ({len(line_items)}):")
    for li in sorted(line_items):
        print(f"  {li}")
    all_line_items.update(line_items)
    if "Creative Group" in df.columns:
        cg = df.dropna(subset=["Creative Group"])
        for _, row in cg.iterrows():
            pairs.add((row["Line Item"], row["Creative Group"]))
        creative = cg["Creative Group"].unique()
        print(f"Creative groups ({len(creative)}):")
        for c in sorted(creative):
            print(f"  {c}")
        all_creative_groups.update(creative)

print("\n\n=== ALL UNIQUE LINE ITEMS ===")
for li in sorted(all_line_items):
    print(li)

print("\n\n=== ALL UNIQUE (Line Item, Creative Group) PAIRS ===")
for li, cg in sorted(pairs):
    print(f"  {li} | {cg}")
EOF
```

```bash
cd "/Users/karolinegriesbach/Documents/Innkeepr/Git/evaluation-and-execution-scripts/Evaluations/Tchibo-DV360" && python3 << 'EOF'
import glob
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd

DATA_DIR = Path("20260624")
files = sorted(glob.glob(str(DATA_DIR / "*.xlsx")))
data_list = []
for file in files:
    temp = pd.read_excel(file, skiprows=7)
    temp["source_file"] = Path(file).name
    data_list.append(temp)
df_raw = pd.concat(data_list, ignore_index=True)

line_items = sorted(
    df_raw.loc[df_raw["Line Item"].notna() & (df_raw["Line Item"] != "Totals"), "Line Item"].unique()
)

settings = {}
for line_item in line_items:
    name = line_item.lower()
    if "kids" in name:
        category = "Kids"
    elif "ladies" in name or "ret_innkeepr" in name:
        category = "Ladies"
    elif "body" in name:
        category = "Body"
    else:
        category = "Other"
    settings.setdefault(category, []).append(line_item)

campaign_column = "Creative Group"
creative_groups = sorted(df_raw.loc[df_raw[campaign_column].notna(), campaign_column].unique())
settings_by_creative = {}
for creative_group in creative_groups:
    category = creative_group.split(" - ")[1]
    settings_by_creative.setdefault(category, []).append(creative_group)

print("line_items:", line_items)
print("settings:", settings)
print("settings_by_creative:", settings_by_creative)

cost_column = "Costs (Total)"
df = df_raw[df_raw[campaign_column].notna() & df_raw["Week"].notna()].copy()
df_line_items = df_raw[
    df_raw["Line Item"].notna()
    & df_raw["Week"].notna()
    & df_raw[campaign_column].isna()
    & (df_raw["Line Item"] != "Totals")
].copy()

print("df creative rows:", len(df))
print("df line item rows:", len(df_line_items))
print("Ladies creative campaigns:", settings_by_creative.get("Ladies"))
print("Ladies line items:", settings.get("Ladies"))
EOF
```

```
DATA_DIR = Path("20260624")
files = sorted(glob.glob(str(DATA_DIR / "*.xlsx")))

data_list = []
for file in files:
    print(f"Read file {file}")
    temp = pd.read_excel(file, skiprows=7)
    temp["source_file"] = Path(file).name
    data_list.append(temp)
    print(temp.shape)

df_raw = pd.concat(data_list, ignore_index=True)

line_items = sorted(
    df_raw.loc[df_raw["Line Item"].notna() & (df_raw["Line Item"] != "Totals"), "Line Item"].unique()
)

settings = {}
for line_item in line_items:
    name = line_item.lower()
    if "ret_" in name:
        category = "RTG"
    elif "per_" in name:
        category = "Seed"
    elif "kids" in name:
        category = "Kids"
    elif "body" in name:
        category = "Body"
    else:
        category = "Other"
    settings.setdefault(category, []).append(line_item)

campaign_column = "Creative Group"
creative_groups = sorted(df_raw.loc[df_raw[campaign_column].notna(), campaign_column].unique())
settings_by_creative = {}
for creative_group in creative_groups:
    category = creative_group.split(" - ")[2].split()[0]
    settings_by_creative.setdefault(category, []).append(creative_group)

print("Unique line items:", line_items)
print("Settings:", settings)
print("Settings by creative group:", settings_by_creative)

```

```bash
import glob
import pandas as pd
from pathlib import Path

files = sorted(glob.glob("*.csv") + glob.glob("*.xlsx"))
data_list = []
for file in files:
    if file.endswith('.csv'):
        skip_rows = 6 if "Innkeepr_Criteo_Jan2026" in file else 7
        temp = pd.read_csv(file, sep=";", skiprows=skip_rows)
    else:
        temp = pd.read_excel(file, skiprows=7)
    temp["source_file"] = Path(file).name
    data_list.append(temp)
df_raw = pd.concat(data_list, ignore_index=True)
use_columns = [col for col in df_raw.columns if "Unnamed" not in col]
df_raw = df_raw[use_columns].dropna(subset=["Line Item"])
df_raw = df_raw.drop_duplicates(subset=["Line Item", "Week"], keep="last")

# Parse CDR

print("CDR dtype mix:")
print("object:", (cdr.dtype == object))
sample = df_raw[["Tchibo CDR Net", "source_file"]].dropna().head(10)
print(sample)

def parse_cdr(series):
    if series.dtype == object:
        s = series.astype(str).str.replace("%", "", regex=False).str.replace(".", "", regex=False).str.replace(",", ".", regex=False).replace({"nan": None})
        s = pd.to_numeric(s, errors="coerce")
    else:
        s = pd.to_numeric(series, errors="coerce")
    # normalize: if any value > 1, assume percentage scale
    if s.max() > 1:
        s = s / 100
    return s

parsed = parse_cdr(df_raw["Tchibo CDR Net"])
print("\nParsed CDR range:", parsed.min(), parsed.max())
print(parsed.describe())
```

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
The xlsx file contains a ratio value of 0.17, while the CSV file contains a percentage value of 17.

A global normalization error was identified: dividing all values by 100 whenever any exceeds 1 incorrectly scales small ratios like 0.17 down to 0.0017. Per-row or per-source normalization is needed instead. CSV cost strings use comma formatting, while xlsx stores floats directly. Revenue data is unavailable.

Revenue cannot be derived from Costs and CDR alone, since that would make ROAS identical to CDR. Without an actual revenue column, the Revenue and ROAS panels will be omitted. The Criteo notebook will use two panels: Costs and CDR. This keeps the structure cleaner than a four-panel layout.

**Data loading**

- Revenue/ROAS panels are included only if a revenue column exists (currently not in Criteo exports)

**Plots**
- **RTG** cell: Costs + CDR (and Revenue + ROAS when available)
- **Seed** cell: same layout
- ROAS plots include the horizontal line at y = 1 when revenue data is present

```bash
import pandas as pd
import glob
from pathlib import Path

files = sorted(glob.glob("*.xlsx"))
for f in files:
    print(f"\n=== {f} ===")
    df = pd.read_excel(f, skiprows=7)

    for column in [cost_column, revenue_column, "Tchibo CDR Net"]:
```

            series.astype(str)

```bash
cd "/Users/karolinegriesbach/Documents/Innkeepr/Git/evaluation-and-execution-scripts/Evaluations/Tchibo-DV360" && python3 << 'EOF'
import glob
from pathlib import Path
import pandas as pd

DATA_DIR = Path("20260624")
files = sorted(glob.glob(str(DATA_DIR / "*.xlsx")))
df_raw = pd.concat([pd.read_excel(f, skiprows=7).assign(source_file=Path(f).name) for f in files], ignore_index=True)
campaign_column = "Creative Group"
cost_column = "Costs (Total)"
revenue_column = "Revenue (Original, DDA Enhanced, ToCnv)"

def parse_numeric(series):
    if series.dtype == object:
        return (
            series.astype(str).str.replace("\xa0", "", regex=False).str.replace("%", "", regex=False)
            .str.replace(".", "", regex=False).str.replace(",", ".", regex=False)
            .replace({"nan": None}).astype(float)
        )
    return pd.to_numeric(series, errors="coerce")

def parse_cdr(series):
    cdr = parse_numeric(series)
    if cdr.max(skipna=True) <= 10:
        cdr = cdr * 100
    return cdr

df = df_raw[df_raw[campaign_column].notna() & df_raw["Week"].notna()].copy()
df["CDR"] = parse_cdr(df["Tchibo CDR Net"])

print("Before -> After (sample):")
sample = df[["Creative Group", "Week", "Tchibo CDR Net", "CDR"]].dropna(subset=["Tchibo CDR Net"]).head(8)
print(sample.to_string())
print(f"\nCDR range: {df['CDR'].min():.2f} - {df['CDR'].max():.2f}")
EOF
```

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

`build_treatment_conversion_match_sql` now accepts `all_treatments=False`. When `True`, it drops the `WHERE treatment IN (...)` filter and returns all treatment/conversion counts from the features table.

**CLI flag:** `--all-treatments`

**Example (Tchibo):**
```bash
python DataChecks/conversion_treatment_match/signal_treatment_conversion_match.py \
  --customer Tchibo \
  --signal-id 68b69fe02e5f2d9a58ce5239 \
  --outlook 30 \
  --all-treatments
```

**Outputs:**
- `signal_treatment_conversion_match_raw.csv` — full SQL result (all treatments × conversion events)
- `signal_treatment_conversion_match.csv` — filtered to the signal’s treatments + goal conversion events
- `signal_treatment_conversion_match_summary.csv` — per-treatment summary

The hardcoded `raw_result.csv` in the repo root is replaced by the `_raw` output next to your `--output` path. Raw results are always saved; with `--all-treatments` the raw file contains the full table counts.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
MongoDB API queries use ISO 8601 strings in JSON. The full format is `2026-06-24T15:00:00.000Z`.

Shorter date-only strings like `2026-06-24` work for `$gte` and `$lt` filters. Raw MongoDB shell queries use `ISODate()`. Some notebooks convert dates to millisecond timestamps instead. The Z suffix marks UTC.
</details></think>

_**Agent (composer-2.5)**_

In this repo, Mongo/API date filters use **ISO 8601 UTC strings** — not raw `ISODate()` objects in Python.

Your example is the right shape:

```text
2026-06-24T15:00:00.000Z
│          │ │        │ │
date       T time     ms Z = UTC
```

**In a query payload (Python):**

```python
content = {
    "created": {
        "$gte": "2026-06-24T15:00:00.000Z",
        "$lt": "2026-06-25T00:00:00.000Z",
    }
}
```

That matches how `check_profiles_via_api.ipynb` does it:

```python
min_date = "2025-12-22T00:00:00.000Z"
{col_last_modified: {"$gte": min_date}}
```

**Common variants in this codebase:**

| Format | Example | Used for |
|--------|---------|----------|
| Full ISO with ms | `"2026-06-24T15:00:00.000Z"` | Precise time filters |
| ISO without ms | `"2026-06-24T15:00:00Z"` | Also valid (`debug_failed_retraining.py`) |
| Date only | `"2026-06-24"` | Day ranges in `check_sessions.ipynb` |

**Generate in Python:**

```python
from datetime import datetime, timezone

dt = datetime(2026, 6, 24, 15, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.") + f"{dt.microsecond // 1000:03d}Z"
# -> '2026-06-24T15:00:00.000Z'
```

**In Mongo shell** (not used directly from these notebooks):

```javascript
{ created: { $gte: ISODate("2026-06-24T15:00:00.000Z") } }
```

Some older notebooks use **millisecond timestamps** instead (`transform_date_to_timestamp_milliseconds`), but the targeting API queries you’re using (`sessions/query`, `profiles/query`) expect the ISO string form above.
